name: Kalambo Falls notched interlocking timbers
description: Two shaped timbers joined across one another by a cut notch provide evidence of structural woodworking.

impact.note: Two joined timbers show structural woodworking at one riverside site, isolated in time with nothing later known to rest on it.

date.label: At least approximately 476,000 ± 23,000 years ago
date.basis: Approximate one-sided younger bound derived from the 476 ± 23 kyr sediment-cluster estimate. The uncertainty is 1σ, not a firm limit; a fading correction would give an older age.

events.statement: Luminescence dating of the deposit associated with the interlocking logs is reported as at least 476 ± 23 thousand years ago.

evidence.locator: pp. 107–109, abstract and BLB5 structural element
evidence.supports: Luminescence dating of the deposit associated with the interlocking logs is reported as at least 476 ± 23 thousand years ago.

evidence.locator: pp. 107–109, abstract and BLB5 structural element

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced event for this particular case, not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The authors report the deposit as at least 476 ± 23 thousand years old. The derived younger endpoint reflects a 1σ uncertainty, not a certain age limit; the paper reports an older estimate if a fading correction is applied. Wood function and hominin species remain uncertain.

research.note: Independent source review checked the structure, luminescence age and excavation unit BLB5; the age is not an occupation interval.
